effect_size.excerpt: Dietary GI, GL, II or fiber were not associated with risk of total or subgroups of prostate cancer. We observed a positive association between dietary intake of whole grains and total prostate cancer (HR highest versus lowest quintile 1.13, 95% CI 1.03–1.24), which was attenuated after restriction to PSA-screened participants (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.91–1.17).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We observed a positive association between dietary intake of whole grains and total prostate cancer (HR highest versus lowest quintile 1.13, 95% CI 1.03–1.24), which was attenuated after restriction to PSA-screened participants (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.91–1.17).

p_value.excerpt: We observed a statistically significant positive association between whole-grain intake and risk of total prostate cancer (HR highest versus lowest quintile 1.13, 95% CI 1.03–1.24, p-trend=0.001) as well as for organ-confined, high-grade and low-grade prostate cancer, but not for advanced prostate cancer.
